protocol: Apple M4 Pro, CPython 3.13.5. Both official macOS arm64 wheels rerun in an interleaved sweep with the same dependencies, images, masks, PONI geometry, 2,000 uniform 2theta bins, polarization 0.965 and solid-angle correction. Pilatus1M: 32 stored copies of one image; Eiger9M: 16 distinct real images. Each timed batch has 56 float64 frame references already in memory. Full CSR and bbox CSR are separate methods. One separate integrator and initialized CSR engine per persistent Python frame worker, with shared geometry arrays; 1/2/4/8 workers, OMP_NUM_THREADS=1, no GPU. Two fresh-process trials per point; three warm timing blocks targeting 0.5 s; intensity and Poisson modes. Imports, pool configuration and input warm-up are outside setup. Lazy imports reached inside pyFAI.load remain included in the constructor time. Constructor and post-constructor components are also recorded in the CSV. Setup measures construction, geometry/CSR initialization and a first Poisson result on every worker, initialized sequentially. Time to first result is also recorded. External RSS sampled every 10 ms, with live heap, USS and physical footprint separately. RSS includes input pages and allocator retention. Both error modes must pass the same <=3.6 other busy logical cores screen. No allocator overrides. All worker-count outputs checked against each version’s own one-worker reference. Version differences compare all 56 output patterns, including all 16 real Eiger images. Dioptrin/azint results displayed from the previously completed qualified sweep, not rerun here. Plot whiskers show the two-trial range, not statistical confidence intervals. This is a CPU/Python comparison and does not assess pyFAI GPU or other integration backends.
